newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-BASF profits up but still disappoint.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-BASF profits up but still disappoint.

text.p: German chemicals group BASF AG on Thursday announced a rise of nearly six percent in first-half pre-tax profits, but still failed to live up to the market's high expectations.
Pre-tax profits rose to 2.46 billion marks ($1.3 billion) from 2.32 billion, although a higher-than-expected tax charge meant net income grew more slowly, up 3.4 percent to 1.42 billion marks.

Sales jumped 14.5 percent to 27.8 billion marks, with the mark's decline against the dollar boosting sales by 900 million marks. A strong performance in the fast-growing oil and gas business in Germany also boosted results.

Although sales met market expectations, analysts had been looking for pre-tax profit of up to 2.53 billion marks, and the group's shares slipped by nearly five percent in early afternoon trading in Frankfurt.
BASF shares were down 3.53 marks at 68.67, dragging shares in rivals Hoechst AG, down 4.90 marks at 76.10, and Bayer AG, off 1.55 marks at 74.25, in their wake.
"Hoechst was not particularly good and now BASF had no ace up its sleeve either," said one Frankfurt dealer.
As part of BASF's efforts to underline its pedigree as a European player rather than a purely German one, the executive board again presented the interim results in London.
Executive board chairman Juergen Strube told a news conference the group was on target to achieve its goal of full-year sales of more than 50 billion marks and lift earnings.
But he warned that while the stronger dollar helps BASF's sales it also made raw materials more expensive. "Therefore margins will not follow sales increases," he said.

Strongest performances were seen at colorants and finishing products, where operating income more than doubled to 411 million marks, boosted by last year's acquisition of Zeneca Group Plc's colours operation.
Oil and gas income jumped by nearly 33 percent to 482 million marks and in the difficult chemicals market, income was up nine percent to 817 million marks.

Analysts said however currency gains were offset by a weak performance in plastics, where price competition helped push income down 43 percent. Health and nutrition was also under pressure due to competition and launch costs for new drugs.

"I can see oil and gas and colorants continuing reasonably strong in the second half. There will be more pressure on the plastics sector, but health and nutrition will see the benefits new products in the U.S.," said analyst Michael Stone at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.

Strube indicated the group could rethink its opposition to floating off or selling parts of the business. It has been under considerable pressure to either get rid of or enlarge its relatively small scale drugs operation in particular.
"If a specific situation arises where something of the highest strategic importance could be reached by divesting or floating part on the stock exchange, we would reconsider," Strube said.
